w: The murti-pratishtha ceremony of a new Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Mandir was performed by Swamishri.

After the opening of two modern libraries and a science laboratory at an educational complex, Swamishri blessed the gathering, saying, "... There is a need for an increase in educational activities in our society, but coupled with education one equally needs moral education. In our ancient Gurukul system, the students were taught spirituality along with their mundane education. If you have a balance of these two then there will be a holistic development. Just as when someone does not have one eye then it is a loss. Similarly, one requires two things - spiritual knowledge and educational knowledge!"

After performing the murti-pratishtha ceremony of a new Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Mandir at Kadodara, Swamishri spoke eloquently on the importance and effect of mandirs, "... When we visited Mauritius we saw that Indians, who had left India several hundred years ago, were following the Hindu dharma. Their forefathers had established 300 mandirs for the preservation of Hindu dharma. Today we find that the Hindu dharma is still being practiced. They have faith and read the Ramayana.

"People from Uttar Pradesh and South India had migrated several hundred years ago to Trinidad. They built mandirs there and preserved their dharma. One should have dharma firmly in one’s life. Those who have dharma in their lives feel they should build mandirs..."
The glory and power of Satsang is that one who comes to Satsang achieves progress, becomes pious and pure and God-conscious.
By obeying God’s instructions one achieves the highest status.
Just as one eats every day and uses one’s home daily, likewise one should chant the name of God daily.

The evening assembly commenced in the Indian Embassy auditorium. After discourses and bhajans, Swamishri finally blessed the audience, saying, "This human birth has been given for offering devotion to God and attaining liberation, but not to indulge and enjoy the worldly pleasures. The worst misery in life is that of birth and death (janma-maran). No one can remedy mental anguish. It is God only who protects one from such pain and misery. As long as there is igorance one has to suffer the cycles of birth and death. This ignorance means 'I'ness and 'Mine'ness... "The body requires food to survive. Similarly, to 'survive', the atma's food is 'bhakti' for God. Through 'bhakti' it acquires strength and grows spiritually. When one attains a God-communion sadhu, only then does one become liberated from 'I'ness and attain atma - realization. Thereafter, by offering bhakti to God does he attain liberation and eternal happiness..."
Swamishri blessed 30 kishores who had pilgrimaged by foot from Botad to Sarangpur and 15 children who had walked 15 km from the village of Vavdi.

In the evening, Swamishri arrived at the grounds of Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir to celebrate the 221st birthday celebration of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. The beautiful stage backdrop, created by sadhus, vividly illustrated the verse from Muktanand Swami's bhajan, "Preme pragtya re suraj Sahajanand, adharma andharu taliyu ..." The giant cut-out of the sun with the divine face of Bhagwan Swaminarayan formed the center of the stage backdrop. The left side was depicted with darkness and evil, namely, demons, bawas who were depraved and slaves to addictions, uncivil customs like widow burning, etc. On the right side, with the arrival of Sahajanand Swami - the dawning sun - the darkness of evil vanished and the luster of goodness was revived. This was symbolized through cut-outs of heaven-kissing mandirs built by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the essence of the Hindu shastras that He distilled and gave in the form of the Vachanamrut, Shikshapatri, and 500 paramahansas (cut-outs of sadhus) and a flourshing tree. The celebration assembly commenced with dhun and prayer, followed by a speech by Pujya Ghanshyamcharan Swami. A beautiful folk dance was performed by children on the bhajan "Ghanshyam, Ghanshyam mari sathe ramva avsho ke nahi ..." Then Pujya Viveksagar Swami brilliantly narrated the life, work and glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. This was followed by a colorful folk dance presentation by kishores on the bhajan "Chaitra sud navmi avi ..." In his blessings, Swamishri said, "Today is a day of great rejoicement and joy for the people of India because it is the birthday of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Bhagwan Shri Ram. Bhagwan Swaminarayan came from Akshardham with a resolve to redeem people. "Just as there is a necessity of schools and colleges in society, there is also the need for sadhus, mandirs and scriptures.What will happen if you have wonderful colleges but no professors! Just as we need professors we also need sadhus to teach and show us the path of righteousness. Bhagwan Swaminarayan came on earth to purify us from our unrighteous thoughts and evil tendencies and He brought Gunatitanand Swami with Him ... "Bhagwan Swaminarayan never advocated proselitization but endeavored in transforming the base natures in people ... One must be proud of one's faith and strive for the progress of one's country. If there is harmony, brotherhood and unity in the country, then there will be peace. And God and his holy sadhus are the way to peace ... "We pray for peace in Gujarat. May the evil tendencies vanish in people's hearts and goodness prevail in their actions ..." Thereafter, Swamishri ceremoniously bathed Shri Harikrishna Maharaj with panchamrut and water and performed pujan amidst the chanting of Vedic mantras by sadhus. At 10.10 p.m., Swamishri performed the arti of Thakorji and then rocked Thakorji in a beautiful hindolo. The spirit of celebration peaked during the singing of festive bhajans, 'Dharma gher anand bhayo ...' and 'Sonana bor jhule Dharmakishor ...' and dancing by children, youths and sadhus. Swamishri gestured and responded happily while the sadhus sang the bhajans. Swamishri was very happy and expressed his satisfaction at the entire celebration.
At 10.30 Swamishri performed the foundation-stone laying ceremony of a new assembly hall for the Swaminarayan hari mandir in Talaja.
At 5.20 p.m. Swamishri departed from Talaja and ten minutes later arrived at the village of Lilavav and blessed the devotees.

At 5.50 p.m. Swamishri arrived at Khandhera and performed the pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti of a 3-shikhar mandir where the murtis of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Laxmi Narayan Dev and Radha Krishna Dev had been installed. After blessing the assembly, Swamishri departed and sanctified a farm in the village of Nagdhanimba near Bhavnagar city.
At 7.40 p.m. Swamishri arrived at Bhavnagar and after darshan at the hari mandir blessed the satsang assembly.
Swamishri performed pujan and arti of the murtis to be installed in a Sanskardham in a suburb of Mahesana.

During the meetings, a seeker broke down sobbing the moment he came before Swamishri. Until now he had worked against Swamishri's mission. Today he had come for darshan for the first time. Confessing openly in front of everyone, he said, "I have worked against you a great deal, but today I feel I did very wrong. Please forgive me."

Calming him, Swamishri said, "Forget whatever happened before. It happens out of ignorance, but forget it. Now keep doing satsang. Remember God as you work. God has forgiven you. What is done in ignorance is not a fault. My blessings are that you and your family are happy. You live nearby, so keep coming to the mandir for darshan."

st.t: US Vice President JD Vance Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham New Delhi
w: The Vice President of the United States, Mr. JD Vance, began his maiden official visit to India with a spiritually enriching visit to Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi. He was joined by his wife, Second Lady Usha Vance, and their three children – Ewan, Vivek, and Mirabel.

Upon arrival, the Vance family received a traditional Indian welcome with flower garlands and friendship threads, symbolizing goodwill and unity. On behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, spiritual leader of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, senior swamis Dharmavatsaldas Swami, Brahmaviharidas Swami, and Gnanmunidas Swami warmly greeted the Vice President.

The family was guided through the Akshardham complex, gaining insights into India’s ancient cultural and spiritual heritage of faith, peace, selfless service, and family unity, which the complex embodies through its architecture and exhibitions.

Vice President Vance was presented a personal letter of blessings and prayers from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj. The letter expressed heartfelt gratitude for the visit and special prayers for the well-being of the Vice President and his family, as well as for the continued unity and progress of the United States of America.

As a gesture of friendship, the Vance family was presented with several commemorative gifts, including a model of the Swaminarayan Akshardham mandir, intricately carved wooden elephants, literature about the Swaminarayan Akshardham campuses in New Delhi and Robbinsville (USA), and value-based illustrated storybooks for their children. A framed family photograph taken in front of the mandir was also presented as a special memento.
Reflecting on the experience, Vice President JD Vance wrote in the guest book:

“Thank you all so much for your hospitality and kindness in welcoming me and my family to this beautiful place. It is a great credit to India that you built a beautiful temple with precision and care. Our kids, in particular, loved it. God bless.”

The special visit reflected the deep-rooted friendship and shared ideals between India and the United States. It also underscored the vital role of spiritual and cultural institutions in fostering and promoting dialogue, respect, and harmony between nations and traditions.
